text.p: Here are highlights of stories in the Romanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- SNCFR railway authority plans to increase tariffs by up to 7.0 percent.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Dunapack package maker of Austria plans to invest $16 million to build a cardboard factory in Romania, the paper says.
- Investors in troubled private bank Dacia Felix will get back part of their savings.
ADEVARUL
- The "leu hunger" created by the central bank's tight policies has helped the national currency strenghten a bit, the paper says.
- Wintershall AG of Germany, which plans to invest $100 million to build a gas pipeline in Romania, asked for property rights over the pipeline, the paper says.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania could become the first ex-communist country to restore monarchy, the paper quoted Russian NTV television as reporting.
- The draft of the Romanian-Ukrainian basic treaty was completed, foreign ministry secretary of state Dumitru Ciausu says in interview.
- Some 130,000 cases of influenza were registered in the past week.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romanian Orthodox Church protested against cloning experiments, saying they were a breach of the "divine creation of the world," a church spokesman said.
- The Interior Ministry rejected a demand by King Michael's staff to put down "Michael of Romania" in his new Romanian passport. The passport reads now "Michael I".
- King Michael is expected to receive a diplomatic passport on Tuesday, after his meeting with Foreign Minister Adrian Severin, the newspaper says.
ADEVARUL

- President Emil Constantinescu could offer a house for king Michael and his family to live in, just like he did in the case of ex-president Ion Iliescu, National Liberal Party leader Mircea Ionescu-Quintus said.
- Romania is supported by France, Italy, Greece and Turkey in its bid to join NATO, the newspaper says.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Senate chairman Petre Roman will meet King Juan Carlos of Spain on Tuesday, as part of his official visit to Spain. ($= 7,744 lei)
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
